assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's 2001-2003 proposal of magic-wavelength optical lattice trapping removes both Doppler and recoil shifts and so enables clocks with fractional uncertainty far below the caesium standard. Ye's group then realised strontium lattice clocks at the 1e-18 level and showed their reach in precision and many-body physics. The idea is original, clear, and has changed precision spectroscopy and tests of fundamental physics. As an atomic physicist I can judge the atomic-structure side of this (magic wavelengths, systematic shifts) as sound.
assessment.attribution: Katori is the originator of the lattice-clock concept and Ye the leading realiser and improver of it; two laureates form a natural, clean configuration. Other groups (for example at PTB, NIST, SYRTE) contributed, but I do not see a competing claim to the core idea. I cannot independently verify every historical priority detail.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across many laboratories, comparisons of clocks at the 1e-18 level, and active discussion of a redefinition of the second make this mature and timely. The 2005 prize recognised the frequency comb, which is related but distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and with Wineland's 2012 ion-clock work may be weighed by colleagues.
Contributions of other clock groups and of theorists who computed shifts may be undercounted by the two supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect from spin-orbit coupling in graphene and the Z2 classification, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened the field of topological insulators. The discovery is conceptually deep, widely influential and clearly stated; it reorganised the understanding of band insulators.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the decisive theory (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall proposal) and Molenkamp's group the first experimental realisation, which is a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Credit is shared with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and with Moore, Balents, Roy, Fu and Hsieh/Hasan for three-dimensional topological insulators, none of which are among the supplied names here; this is a real allocation difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many independent materials and experiments over about two decades, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The supplied trio omits the HgTe theoretical proposal and the three-dimensional topological insulator work, so the credited set may not map onto all decisive contributions.
This is condensed matter theory outside my own subfield, so I defer to colleagues on priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gives a controlled, non-perturbative treatment of strongly correlated electrons, capturing Mott physics and the interplay of local correlations with band structure. Its combination with density-functional methods is now a standard tool for real materials. The development is original and has lasting methodological impact, and as a many-body theorist I value that it is a quantitatively usable method rather than a model alone.
assessment.attribution: The infinite-dimensional limit was introduced by Metzner and Vollhardt, and the mapping to a self-consistent impurity problem by Georges and Kotliar; Müller-Hartmann also contributed. The supplied names include Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar, which fits the core of the credit, but Metzner is not among them, which leaves some attribution ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, extensive benchmarks and successful application in materials; mature. Some limitations (cluster extensions, non-local correlations) remain active but do not undermine the core achievement.
uncertainties: Metzner and Müller-Hartmann are not in the credited names, so the best three-person configuration is debatable.
The Nobel tradition regarding theory in this area and the direct link to experimental discovery may be questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BB84 protocol and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol established that secure key distribution can rest on quantum mechanics. The idea is simple, original, and has founded a large field with deployed technology and a connection to Bell tests that the 2022 prize recognised from the experimental side.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the originators of BB84, and Ekert of E91; the three supplied names form a plausible trio. Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding is a precedent that complicates priority and he is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: protocols have been realised over fibre and satellite links, and security proofs have progressed, although practical implementation loopholes persist. Recognition is timely, and it complements the 2022 prize.
uncertainties: Wiesner's conjugate coding and later security proofs (Mayers, Lo-Chau, Shor-Preskill) raise credit questions.
Whether cryptography counts as physics for the prize is a possible concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics, the coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, gave strong coupling, dispersive readout and a scalable architecture for superconducting quantum processors. The proposal and first demonstration are original and have had decisive impact on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the architecture in 2004 and Wallraff and Schoelkopf (with the Yale group) demonstrated it; this is a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others, notably Devoret and Girvin, share credit in the Yale effort, which I cannot resolve from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and now industrial, but the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, which makes a closely related prize soon afterwards less likely to be viewed as timely.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may weigh against near-term recognition.
Yale-group credit beyond the supplied names, especially Devoret and Girvin, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise tunable Hubbard-type models. The Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition, followed by quantum gas microscopes, created the field of quantum simulation. This is highly original and conceptually clear, and as an atomic physicist I appreciate the control achieved.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided decisive theory; Greiner and Bloch the Mott insulator experiment and later microscopy; Hänsch is also associated with the Mott experiment. I selected three from the four supplied names; Cirac's role is substantial but I chose to avoid dilution, which is a judgement call. Jaksch is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature as an experimental platform with many independent groups, though practical quantum advantage in simulation is still under development, and parts of the credit sit near the already-recognised BEC prize area (2001).
uncertainties: Choice between Cirac and Greiner or Bloch among the four supplied names is not obvious.
Jaksch and Hänsch contributions are not among the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction made fault-tolerant quantum computation conceptually possible by showing errors can be corrected without measuring the data. Shor's code, Steane's code and Kitaev's topological codes are original and fundamental, and recent below-threshold experiments strengthen the relevance.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane each independently discovered the first codes, and Kitaev introduced topological codes; others (Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme) are also central. The supplied triple is defensible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Theory is mature, while experimental demonstration of scalable logical qubits is recent and ongoing, so the physical confirmation is still developing; recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Experimental validation of fault tolerance at scale is incomplete.
Missing names such as Gottesman, Calderbank and Knill complicate the credit; the work is close to computer science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The realisation of strongly interacting Fermi gases, the BEC-BCS crossover, molecular condensates and the unitary gas, offers a clean testbed for many-body physics from superfluidity to neutron-star-related matter. The work is important and quantitatively precise, and it connects with my interest in few- and many-body systems.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Salomon and Zwierlein are leading experimentalists among the supplied names; the molecular BEC from fermions was realised nearly simultaneously by several groups (Jin's group, Grimm, Ketterle, Salomon), and Deborah Jin is deceased. The allocation is quite unclear.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups for two decades, but simultaneous discovery and the death of a key figure make a fair configuration difficult, and the topic is close to previously honoured ultracold gas prizes.
uncertainties: Simultaneous independent realisations and the absence of Jin and Ketterle from the credited names make attribution unstable.
Distinguish whether the main discovery is the molecular BEC, the crossover, or the unitary-gas studies.
